summary.headline: JK Tyre Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs.4,850 crore (+20% YoY), with EBITDA margin up to 7.1% from 6.8% despite raw material inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record Rs.4,850 crore, up 20% YoY from Rs.4,026 crore, with domestic volumes up 22% and OE up 25%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 28% QoQ to Rs.343 crore and PAT to Rs.60 crore, as NSR increases of about 7% QoQ offset a further ~9% QoQ rise in raw material costs. Net debt rose Rs.751 crore QoQ to Rs.5,696 crore on working capital for higher RM prices and capex. Management guided to a further 4-5% RM basket increase and 4-5% NSR increase in Q3.

financial_highlights.change: described as significant improvement; no prior-period figures stated

segments.name: India domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes up 22% YoY, with OE up 25% and replacement up 20%; domestic revenue up 32% YoY, with OE sales up 65% post GST 2.0. Domestic volumes rose about 13% QoQ, split equally between volume and NSR.

segments.name: TBR (truck-bus radial)
segments.commentary: OE volumes up 76% YoY and replacement up 9% YoY; management cites category growth of high single digits in the medium term.

segments.name: PLR / PCR (passenger car radial)
segments.commentary: PLR volumes up 14% overall, led by OE growth of 35% YoY; PLR is 28% of standalone revenue. Around 30% of passenger line H1 volumes are 16-inch and above premium SKUs, a segment growing about 20% CAGR over 2-3 years.

segments.name: Farm, 2/3W and EV
segments.commentary: Farm volumes up 16% in replacement and 6% in OE, with farm exports up 11% YoY. 2/3W volumes up 34% YoY, with replacement more than 2x. EV volumes up 24% QoQ.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.479 crore and EBITDA Rs.23 crore in Q2 as operations resumed; OEM volumes to the US expected to return to last-year levels in Q3-Q4, and Mexico-to-US exports grew triple-digit QoQ in volume.

guidance_outlook: Raw material basket expected to rise a further 4-5% in Q3 FY27, with a similar range hoped for in Q4; management sees no availability issue.
NSR planned to rise a further 4-5% in Q3 FY27, after about 7% QoQ in Q2 and 4-5% in Q1 (11-12% cumulative over six months).
Remaining FY27 capex guided at about Rs.500 crore, against Rs.1,200 crore full-year guidance and Rs.800 crore spent so far.
Expansion projects of Rs.1,130 crore are underway, with a further phased capex of about Rs.5,000 crore to follow; asset turn expected at 1:1.1.
Margin improvement expected in Q3 as cost efficiencies and OEM index-led price pass-through lag catch up; replacement pass-through is constrained by competition.
Demand expected steady in Q3 and supported by OEM year-end closing in Q4; farm season could face pressure from rain deficit.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation in India above 90% across key segments including TBR, PLR and 2/3W.
Rs.1,400 crore of projects recently completed, per CFO; further expansion for TBR and PCR underway.
Rs.1,130 crore expansion currently under way, followed by phased capex of about Rs.5,000 crore.
FY27 capex: about Rs.800 crore spent in H1, with about Rs.500 crore more planned for the balance of the year.
JK Tornel upgradation-cum-modernisation expansion progressing as planned.
demand_pricing: Raw material basket up about 9% QoQ in Q2, after 22% in Q1; cumulative increase of about 30% over six months. Crude-linked inputs are about 65-70% of RM.
NSR up about 7% QoQ in Q2, after 4-5% in Q1; 11-12% cumulative over six months.
OEM pricing is index-led with a lag; replacement pass-through is constrained by competition.
Replacement market mix 60%, OE 30%, exports 10% of standalone revenue. Category mix: truck and bus about 56%, PLR 28%, 2/3W 6%, non-truck-bias 10%.
Exports from India up 14% QoQ; Q2 exports of farm category up 11% YoY.
Industry growth in H1 FY27 was strong (CV +30%, PV +26%, 2/3W +27% YoY in Q2), attributed to GST 2.0, festive season and freight growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation by item (carbon black, rubber, steel cord) and the ability to pass it on?
qa_highlights.answer: The RM basket rose 9% QoQ and about 30% over six months; crude-based inputs (carbon black, synthetic rubber, butyl, steel cord) are 65-70% of RM. Q3 basket guidance is +4-5%, NSR is +4-5%, and there is no availability issue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone and consolidated cost trends diverge, and how does the Mexico billing work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TBR is manufactured in India and sold to the Mexico subsidiary, which bills LATAM and Mexican domestic customers. Transfer pricing is on an arm's length basis. The subsidiary is not directly sold to by India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise and what is the capex and net debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt rose on about 30% higher RM values in inventory, higher volumes and capex-led borrowings for TBR/PCR expansion. Remaining FY27 capex is about Rs.500 crore, and inventory is expected to ease with operating efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume growth from capex be quantified, and have non-crude RM prices peaked?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is expected to add revenue at about a 1:1.1 asset turn. Management gave no peak call, but expects a 4-5% basket increase every quarter, driven by crude-based inputs and natural rubber.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise to Rs.743 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher RM prices (about 30% in six months), volume growth, and deliberate strategic raw material inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory for Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not commit to a numerical path. It said there is unabsorbed cost from RM inflation, OEM price increases lag, and it expects some basis-point margin improvement in Q3.

risks_watch: RM inflation: basket up 30% in six months; further 4-5% guided for Q3, with Q4 uncertain and tied to West Asia conflict and crude prices.
Unabsorbed cost and replacement-market pass-through lag may keep margins below management's expectations.
Working capital and leverage: net debt Rs.5,696 crore, net debt to equity 0.94x; FCF negative in H1 FY27.
JK Tornel recovery: OEM volumes to the US expected to return to last-year levels in Q3-Q4.
Farm segment could see pressure from a rain deficit and a high H2 base.
Transfer pricing between India and the Mexico subsidiary is under arm's-length scrutiny.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and volumes (record revenue, OE growth, high utilisation), but cautious on margins and cash flow: management acknowledged unabsorbed RM cost and gave no firm margin path. Answers on RM peak timing and Mexico margins were less specific.
key_quotes: Cumulatively, we have seen a staggering 30% increase in the last 6 months.

We are delighted to announce that the recently launched MG hector Tomahawk has been introduced on our EV specific tyre viz. Ranger HPe (18 inch size), reinforcing the strong trust placed in us by the leading OEMs.
So there is a delta, which has been unabsorbed.
In terms of the availability, there is no scarcity or availability issue right now.

growth.why: Management guides NSR up 4-5% and RM basket up 4-5% in Q3 FY27 with Rs.1,130 crore expansion under way and Rs.1,400 crore recently completed, but no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given and the brief's EBITDA growth figure is QoQ (+28%), not YoY, so it is left null.
